⚖️ I want to do something different with this one. Rather than tell you what to think, I'll set out two cases exactly as reported, ask an honest question, and genuinely ask for YOUR view.

👮 Case one: a suspended councillor in Birmingham, charged with five assault offences — including the alleged assault of three police officers — granted UNCONDITIONAL BAIL, trial next year.

⛵ Case two: the activist Danny Tommo, REMANDED IN CUSTODY after denying criminal damage over the alleged slashing of a dinghy, bail refused, trial next year.

Let me be completely clear, because it's right: BOTH deny the charges. Both are entitled to the presumption of innocence and a fair trial. Neither has been convicted. Bail and remand are decided by the courts on legal tests, and in the Tommo case the judge said he set political motivations aside. These are live cases and the courts decide them — not me, and I'm not saying any single decision was wrong.

But set them side by side, as any ordinary person will, and ask honestly: how does an alleged assault on three serving police officers end in unconditional bail, while an allegation of damaging a boat ends in a cell? Yes, they're different charges. But can you see why so many people look at those two outcomes and ask whether we really do have one law for everyone? Nigel Farage and others have asked the same thing.

Justice doesn't only have to be done — it has to be SEEN to be done. When people feel the treatment depends on who you are or what you believe, faith in the whole system drains away.

So I'm asking you, genuinely: what do you make of it? Does it feel even-handed? Are assaults on police taken seriously enough? Does the system treat everyone the same?

Tell me honestly in the comments — I'd rather represent what you actually think than assume it. For my part, I'll always back our police, and I'll always argue for one law, applied equally to all.
